name: What happens to the flooring where the wall used to be?

mainEntity.name: What happens to the flooring where the wall used to be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flooring continuity is not automatic after a wall is removed. The former wall footprint may lack finished flooring, and adjacent materials may be discontinued, damaged, uneven, or installed at different heights. Context: Matching can require a repair strip, refinishing, replacement across a larger area, or a deliberate transition that becomes part of the design. Key factors: existing material; age and availability; subfloor height; cabinetry sequence. Practical guidance: Inspect flooring before demolition and ask for both a matching strategy and a replacement alternative in the estimate. Decide whether cabinets, island, or a threshold can conceal unavoidable transitions. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate flooring with the broader kitchen or whole-home finish plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: The area may have unfinished or mismatched flooring, and the existing material may be unavailable or damaged. Inspect it before demolition and price several solutions: repair strip, refinishing, replacement across a larger area, or a planned transition under cabinetry or between zones.
